newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil firm, outlook buoyant on tightness.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil firm, outlook buoyant on tightness.

text.p: The market failed to respond noticeably to the details of the EdP tender that filtered out in the afternoon.
One trader was understood to have secured six cargoes at around mean fob NWE, mean fob Med +$10.50-70 cif Portugal.
"It's not much of a surprise (the price) and I think they (the winner) probably have some stuff already," a trader said. There was no information about the two optional Oct cargoes.
In the morning a trader sold a high sulphur cargo to an end-user at a p and c level that was believed to be at high cif NWE.
Dealers said prices could ease in the first part of September, to allow cargoes to be bought, and then rise in readiness for delivery dates.

Low sulphur cracked fuel was also steady. A trader was heard looking for 50,000 tonnes at $105.50 fob NWE. There was market speculation the requirement was for a Med buyer, but this was denied. Some dealers thought the main Med buyer had already discreetly secured a spot cargo.
The tone was firm with a Danish utility understood to be in the market for up to three parcels of around 25,000 tonnes in September. -- Matthew Jones, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8980
